# Starter maintenance

A stiff-ish white starter kept at 100 % hydration is the reference culture: equal weights flour and water, fed at a 1:5:5 ratio (one part starter, five parts flour, five parts water).

## Feed ratios and timing

| Ratio | 21 °C | 26 °C |
|---|---|---|
| 1:1:1 | 3–4 h to peak | 2–2.5 h |
| 1:5:5 | 6–8 h to peak | 4–5 h |
| 1:10:10 | 10–12 h to peak | 7–8 h |

Peak is the point of maximum rise, just before the dome flattens. A starter roughly triples on a 1:5:5 feed. Use it within 2 hours either side of peak; past that, acidity climbs and the culture drags the [bulk fermentation](bulk-fermentation.md) out by an hour or more.

## Reading the culture

- **Domed and bubbly, faintly sweet-sour** — at peak, ready.
- **Flat top with a liquid layer (hooch)** — hungry by several hours; feed twice before baking.
- **Sharp acetone smell** — badly under-fed; two 1:5:5 feeds 12 h apart restore it.

## Storage

Fridge at 4 °C holds a fed starter for 7–10 days. Bring it back with two feeds at room temperature; the second should peak on schedule before you trust it in a dough.

Flour choice matters less than consistency, but a 10–20 % wholemeal fraction in the feed speeds the peak by roughly an hour at 21 °C — the same absorption effect described in [hydration](hydration.md).
